questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good weather, international environment, and strong academic reputation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing experience with great weather, many international friends, and big improvement in my English.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Most information was shared by email before arrival, but keep in mind that Católica answers slowly, so you need to be patient and pro-active.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction meetings, campus tour, and help from international coordinators.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Staff were friendly and helpful (but slow)!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Many options in the city, but start looking early.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is quite expensive to live in Lisbon. I would start looking early and check Idealista or Facebook groups like ‘Rent an apartment in Lisbon’.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The system was slow and the administration had a clear procedure for the one-year LLM programme, but less clear structures for exchange students. I had to email and meet with the administration many times to choose my courses (30 ECTS) for the semester, and some popular courses filled up quickly. However, the staff were very kind and helpful when speaking with them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration was done online before the semester started, but you could edit your choices once you arrived.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help by email from the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to change most of my initially preferred courses after arrival.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register as early as possible and don’t get frustrated. The university is not always certain which courses will run in your semester when you have to register, so you will most likely need to change your choices once you arrive.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Challenging but manageable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More interactive and discussion-based.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend International Commercial Arbitration and Investment Dispute Resolution and Data Protection Law because they are practical, well-taught and very relevant for an international legal career. The tech courses like Data Science for Lawyers and Law and Automation are also interesting and different from typical law courses at UCPH.

Be aware that you need to take many more courses than in a normal semester at UCPH, because several courses are quite small (often 2 or 4 ECTS). This means more classes and more exams during the semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Higher rent than expected, and eating out a lot (cheaper than in Denmark, but it still adds up in the end)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive, but food, public transport and eating out were cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many activities and events for students at Catolica in general.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports activities, surfing, and weekend trips around Portugal.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfing and weekend trips, because they are fun and a great way to get to know other international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Lisbon, visit the beaches, go to Sintra and Cascais, and travel to Porto and the Algarve.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are open and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in class and group work.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Administrative processes can be slow and less structured.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed lifestyle, the weather and the social atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Start looking for housing early, be patient with the administration, and say yes to social activities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you take courses from the international one-year LLM programme, which I did as a master’s (MA) exchange student, most of your classmates are full-year students who study together for the entire year. I was there in the autumn semester and started at the same time as them, which made it easier to socialize. If you arrive in the spring semester, many of them will already know each other, which can make it a bit harder to integrate socially. You should also be aware that there are not many exchange students in the LLM classes, since most students are full-time fee-paying students on the one-year programme. On the other hand, the environment is very international, with many German and other European students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world and becoming more confident in English.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing and managing many small courses and exams at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Lisbon is a great city for exchange with amazing weather, international atmosphere and lots of opportunities both academically and socially.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
